name: Poor Law Unions 30 Mar 1851
description: The 163 Poor Law Unions of Ireland at the census of 30 Mar 1851, as the 1851 county reports list them under 'Poor Law Unions and Electoral Divisions'. The same unions stood from the declaration of Castletowndelvin on 9 Aug 1850, the last of the 33 unions formed in 1848-50, until Newport was dissolved on 30 Sep 1885. No map of the 1851 electoral divisions exists, so each union is drawn as the 1907-12 District Electoral Divisions (Phelim Birch's and Paddy Matthews's maps) that cover its 1851 divisions, matched by name from hand transcriptions of the printed tables; a division printed as 'part of' is given whole to one union, and town divisions redrawn by 1891 are matched by name. Each union carries its land area (land_acres: the map area less large lakes and tideway, which the census also leaves out), the sum of its printed county-part acreages (census_acres), the difference (pct_diff) and a confidence grade. Of the 157 unions that can be checked, 146 agree within 1% and 153 within 2% (median 0.11%); Belfast (+8.4%, reclaimed foreshore inside the later city wards), Wexford (+4.8%, reclaimed slobs), Londonderry (+4.0%, divisions redrawn round Derry, Coleraine and Limavady) and Donegal (-2.8%, Lough Eask counted by the census) are further out. The King's County divisions are from the 1851 King's County report. Six unions are graded unchecked: the six Dublin unions (Balrothery, Celbridge, Dunshaughlin, North Dublin, Rathdown and South Dublin), which follow the 1891 tables because the CSO file labelled 1851 Dublin is in fact the Queen's County report (so Queen's County is checked and Dublin is not). The map is simplified for display by a coverage simplification of the division map, so neighbouring unions keep common edges (95% of divisions lie within 10 m of the full lines); the full-resolution file is among the downloads.
